summary: Did you know that the arrangement of the Old Testament in Protestant Christian Bibles is not original?

title: Genesis 12-50
summary: Genesis 12–50: Abraham’s family and the promise that runs through the rest of the Bible.

title: Genesis 1-11
summary: Genesis 1–11: creation, rebellion, and the scattering of the nations.

title: Exodus 1-18
summary: Exodus 1–18: slavery, the plagues, Passover and the sea.

title: Exodus 19-40
summary: Exodus 19–40: Sinai, the covenant, the golden calf and the tabernacle.

title: Numbers
summary: Numbers: the wilderness generation.

title: Joshua
summary: The book of Joshua shows us God’s covenant faithfulness to bring the Israelites into the land he promised Abraham.

title: Leviticus
summary: Leviticus: how a holy God can live among a sinful people.

title: Ruth
summary: Ruth: loyalty, redemption and the great-grandmother of David.

title: Judges
summary: After the death of Joshua, the people of Israel begin a downward spiral.The book of Judges highlights six judges and their increasing corruption during this time.

title: Deuteronomy
summary: In the book of Deuteronomy, Moses gives Israel final words of warning and blessing. He covers the story so far, a collection of laws, and a charge for Israel to listen and obey rather than rebel.

title: 1 Samuel
summary: 1 Samuel: Israel asks for a king.

title: Ezra-Nehemiah
summary: Ezra–Nehemiah: the return and rebuilding.

title: 1 & 2 Kings
summary: 1–2 Kings: from Solomon to exile.

title: 2 Samuel
summary: 2 Samuel: David’s reign, rise and failures.

title: Job
summary: Job, his wife, and his friends continually speculate on why an upright man like Job might experience so much suffering. God reminds Job that the world has order and beauty but it is also wild and dangerous.

title: Esther
summary: Though God is never mentioned in the book of Esther, we can see clearly that he is at work behind the scenes, ensuring that Haman’s plot to destroy the Jewish people is thwarted.

title: Psalms
summary: Psalms: the design of the Psalter as one book.

title: Isaiah 1-39
summary: Isaiah 1–39.

title: Song of Songs
summary: Song of Songs.

title: Proverbs
summary: Linked to Solomon and other wise men, the book of Proverbs includes hundreds of short, clever sayings designed to teach us how to live and act wisely.

title: Ecclesiastes
summary: The book of Ecclesiastes is the author’s response to Proverbs. From their perspective, life isn’t so simple as fearing God and choosing wisdom. Life is unpredictable, and our existence is a blip of time.

title: Isaiah 40-66
summary: Isaiah 40–66.

title: Jeremiah
summary: The prophet Jeremiah announced that God would judge Israel’s sins with exile to Babylon. And then he lived through the horror of his predictions.

title: Daniel
summary: Daniel.

title: Lamentations
summary: Lamentations is a collection of poems detailing Israel’s grief after Jerusalem’s destruction, which was caused by their rebellion against God.

title: Ezekiel 1-33
summary: Ezekiel is a prophet living in exile in Babylon. Ezekiel boldly speaks God’s message of Israel’s rebellion and makes clear that this exile is punishment for their covenant unfaithfulness.

title: Hosea
summary: In the book of Hosea, God sends Hosea to Israel during the reign of King Jeroboam II to communicate God’s despair over their perpetual idol worship and dependence on outside nations.

title: Ezekiel 34-48
summary: Ezekiel is a prophet living in exile in Babylon. God’s presence being revealed to Ezekiel demonstrates that holiness has nothing to do with geographical location—it’s about the condition of the heart.

title: Joel
summary: Joel.

title: Obadiah
summary: Obadiah.

title: Jonah
summary: The book of Jonah poses fascinating questions for us to ponder. Do we truly forgive and love our enemies? And do we run from God when faced with our failures?

title: Micah
summary: The prophet Micah describes God’s coming judgment on Israel because it has exploited the poor and twisted the laws of the Torah. But Micah’s prophecies are not without hope.

title: Nahum
summary: The book of Nahum is a collection of poems announcing the downfall of some of Israel’s worst oppressors.

title: Amos
summary: Amos.

title: Zephaniah
summary: The book of Zephaniah contains intense images of God’s justice and hope.

title: Zechariah
summary: Zechariah.

title: Habakkuk
summary: Habakkuk.

title: Malachi
summary: The book of Malachi is a stark indictment of Israel’s rebellion, but it offers a surprising message of hope too. Even after years of rebellion and exile, God has not abandoned Israel.

title: Haggai
summary: Haggai challenges the returning exiles to remember their covenant, remain faithful to God, and build the temple before constructing their own homes.

title: 1 & 2 Chronicles
summary: 1–2 Chronicles: Israel’s story retold after the exile.

title: Matthew 14-28
summary: Matthew 14–28: the road to Jerusalem, the cross and the commission.

title: Matthew 1-13
summary: Matthew 1–13: Jesus as the new Moses who brings God’s kingdom.

title: New Testament Overview
summary: The New Testament is not a separate story. It’s a continuation of the story introduced in the Old Testament and a fulfillment of God’s covenant promises introduced in the first part of the Bible.

title: Mark
summary: Mark: the suffering servant-king.

summary: John 1–12.

summary: Luke 1–9.

summary: Luke 10–24.

summary: Acts 13–28.

title: 1 Corinthians
summary: Paul’s first letter to the Corinthians is a wake-up call: the resurrection gives us a reason for unity, motivation to maintain sexual purity, ability to love other people more than ourselves, and ultimate hope for victory over death.

title: 2 Corinthians
summary: 2 Corinthians.

title: Galatians
summary: In the book of Galatians, followers of Jesus learn that they are justified by the Gospel of Jesus, not the laws of Torah. They are a part of a multi-ethnic family of God and equipped by the Spirit to love God and others.

title: Ephesians
summary: Ephesians.

title: Colossians
summary: The book of Colossians addresses problems the church at Colossae faced, challenging followers of Jesus to examine their lives and be transformed through the resurrection and love of Jesus.

title: Philippians
summary: Philippians.

title: 1 Thessalonians
summary: In 1 Thessalonians, Paul celebrates the Church’s holiness, love, and future hope as they remain faithful to Jesus. Despite persecution, the church has flourished in their faith.

title: Titus
summary: In the book of Titus, Paul reminds Cretan believers that, despite their sinful culture, they can be transformed into a new humanity by the same grace that Jesus demonstrated when he died to redeem them.

title: 2 Thessalonians
summary: In his second letter to the Thessalonians, Paul encourages the church to   remain faithful, hopeful, confident, and fearless while waiting for Jesus’ return and deliverance from the evil ruler.

title: 1 Timothy
summary: 1 Timothy.

title: Philemon
summary: In this book, Paul asks Philemon to forgive his runaway slave, Onesimus. This is a revolutionary act, demonstrating the Gospel in action and showing that all people are equal partners in the new humanity.

title: Hebrews
summary: Hebrews.

title: 2 Timothy
summary: 2 Timothy.

title: James
summary: The book of James is filled with short wisdom speeches that are full of metaphors and easily memorized one-liners. While James doesn’t teach new theology, this book does challenge believers on how they should live.

title: 1 Peter
summary: 1 Peter.

title: 1-3 John
summary: 1–3 John.

title: 2 Peter
summary: In this letter, Peter issues two warnings against corrupt teachers, who are objecting to the reality of Jesus’ resurrection and leading the community astray.

title: Jude
summary: The book of Jude references the Hebrew Bible and Jewish literature to illustrate God’s judgment on rebellion. Jude challenges the church to contend for the faith and stay faithful to God.

title: Revelation 1-11
summary: The book of Revelation is not a secret code for deciphering the timeline of Jesus’ return. It’s a work of apocalyptic literature that shows how every human kingdom eventually becomes Babylon and must be resisted.

title: Revelation 12-22

title: Genesis Part 1: Creation and Chaos
summary: The story of the Bible opens with God creating beauty and order out of chaos and darkness. Will humans trust him to continue to provide?

title: Genesis Part 2: Chosen and Blessed
summary: When humans choose their own desires over trusting God's provision, God begins a rescue plan that starts with one man.

title: Exodus Part 1: Redemption From Slavery
summary: In an epic showdown, God confronts evil and injustice and rescues his people from slavery. How do the people respond to God's faithfulness?

title: Numbers: Wandering in the Wilderness
summary: The people just keep rebelling—and God continually responds with  provision and protection! But the book of Numbers also reveals that God's justice accompanies his mercy.

title: Deuteronomy: Moses’ Final Words
summary: How does Moses say goodbye? The fifth and final book of the Torah contains a collection of speeches from the first Israelite leader urging the next generation’s faithfulness to God.

title: Exodus Part 2: Covenant at Mount Sinai
summary: What does it mean for a nation to belong to God? In the second part of Exodus, God establishes a covenant with his people, Israel, and invites them to access his presence through the tabernacle.

title: Leviticus: Living in God’s Presence
summary: What happens when God moves into the neighborhood? Leviticus outlines the guidance God provides for Israel to experience his presence and reflect his goodness and justice to the world.

title: The Wisdom of Proverbs
summary: What guidance do generations of people offer on living a God-centered life? Explore this collection of sayings intended for re-reading and contemplation.

title: The Wisdom of Ecclesiastes
summary: Why do we often feel out of control in this life? Ecclesiastes addresses the wisdom we need to exist with life’s uncertainties and continually hope for God's rescue.

title: The Wisdom of Job
summary: Is God still just if good people suffer? Explore the surprising answer to this question and how Job and his friends try to make sense of God's role in suffering.

summary: The birth of Jesus in Luke 1–2.

summary: The journey to Jerusalem and the prodigal son (Luke 9–19).

title: Pentecost: Acts 1-7
summary: In this video, we'll explore how God's Spirit filled and empowered Jesus' followers, renewing them and preparing them to announce the good news to the nations.

title: The Resurrection of Jesus: Luke 24
summary: This video concludes Luke's epic portrait of Jesus of Nazareth, setting the stage for his second volume, Acts. The tomb is empty and Jesus is alive, seated as the ruler of God’s Kingdom.

title: The Apostle Paul: Acts 8-12
summary: In this video, we meet the apostle Paul. See how God transformed Paul and grew a small collective of messianic Jews in Jerusalem into a multi-ethnic movement that quickly spread throughout the nations.

title: Paul's Missionary Journeys: Acts 13-20
summary: What was it like for Paul to travel around the Roman Empire announcing the good news about the risen Jesus? How did people respond to his message?

title: Bound for Rome: Acts 21-28
summary: In the final video in our Acts series, we trace Paul’s final journey to Jerusalem and then into a Roman prison.

summary: Jesus begins this collection of teachings with a section often referred to as the Beatitudes. Learn how these surprising statements describe the arrival of God's Kingdom.

summary: Explore an introduction to the largest collection of Jesus' teachings in the first episode of Sermon on the Mount.

summary: Jesus offers a bold vision of doing right that is grounded in God's wisdom. Learn how this vision fulfills the teachings of the Torah.

title: The Lord’s Prayer
summary: In a short prayer, Jesus shows us how to align our desires with the purposes of God’s Kingdom.

summary: Explore how Jesus reveals God’s wisdom underneath Old Testament laws about oaths, revenge, and enemies in the Sermon on the Mount in Matthew 5.

summary: What does religious hypocrisy look like? Explore three examples from Jesus in Matthew 6:1-8 and his warnings about the temptation to become a hypocrite.

title: 2nd Commandment: No Idols
summary: In the ancient world, people created statues known as idols to represent deities and spiritual beings. But in the 2nd Commandment, Yahweh forbids the making of idols of himself or any other spiritual being.

title: The 10 Commandments as Wisdom
summary: The 10 Commandments are among the most well-known rules in the Bible and all of history. But what if they are more than just rules? What if they are a pathway to a universe of wisdom?

title: 3rd Commandment: Do Not Carry the Name in Vain
summary: God forbids Israel to take his name in vain. The most literal translation of “take” is actually “carry.” What is God’s name, and what does it mean to carry it?

title: 1st Commandment: No Other Gods
summary: After Yahweh delivers the people of Israel from slavery in Egypt, he enters into a covenant agreement with them at Mount Sinai.

title: 4th Commandment: Remember the Sabbath
summary: Yahweh commands Israel to stop their laboring and rest on the seventh day of every week. What is the point of this weekly practice, and how can it shape those who follow it?

title: 8th Commandment: Do Not Steal
summary: God forbids Israel from stealing—simple enough. But what underlying beliefs cause someone to steal in the first place? And what is the deeper opportunity beyond simply not taking what belongs to our neighbor?

title: 6th Commandment: Do Not Kill
summary: Most contemporary English translations of the 6th Commandment read, “You shall not murder.” But the Hebrew word used in the commandment refers to ending a life, unrelated to purpose or premeditation.

title: 9th Commandment: Do Not Bear False Witness
summary: A common summary for the 9th Commandment is “Do not lie.” But it actually means “Do not bear false witness against your neighbor,” drawing attention to a specific kind of lying in a public, legal setting.

title: 7th Commandment: Do Not Commit Adultery
summary: God tells Israel not to commit adultery, which involves having sex with someone who is in a marriage covenant. Why is protecting marriage so important to God, and what does marriage ultimately point to?

title: 5th Commandment: Honor Your Father and Mother
summary: Yahweh commands Israel to honor their parents so that they may have long lives in the promised land. Why is there a connection between parents and life in the land, and what does it look like to honor them?

title: 10th Commandment: Do Not Desire Your Neighbor’s Possessions
summary: The 10th Commandment is often translated as “Do not covet,” but the Hebrew simply uses the common word for desire. Why do the 10 Commandments end this way, and how can we desire what is good?

title: Looking Back on the 10 Commandments
summary: In the 10 Commandments, we hear God’s voice and wisdom that can lead us to a deeper, richer life. And each of the commandments invites us to meditate on the story of the Bible in surprising ways.

title: The Wilderness
summary: Why does God sometimes lead his people into harsh and isolated places? Trace the theme of the wilderness through the story of the Bible and discover how trusting God in the wilderness prepares us for life in the garden.

title: Redemption
summary: What if “redemption” means more than making something better? Discover how ancient biblical writers understood it as the cosmic work of rescue—where the creator reclaims his people to bring them home.

title: Anointing
summary: Why oil is poured on people and places: anointing, and what “Messiah” means.

title: The Mountain
summary: Watch a short video that explains what mountains represent in the Bible. Learn the key role mountains play throughout the unified story that leads to Jesus.

title: The City
summary: Why does the Bible open with a garden as the ideal space but close with a heavenly city? Explore the surprising theme of the city in the Bible.

title: The Exodus Way
summary: The story of Israel’s exodus from Egypt can be described as the way out of slavery, the way through the wilderness, and the way into the promised land.

title: Chaos Dragon
summary: In the ancient world, the sea dragon was a common symbol that represented death and chaos. But the story of the Bible begins with God demonstrating his power over all creatures.

title: Eternal Life
summary: Jesus offered people eternal life. But what does that mean? Explore the meaning of a phrase that invites us into God’s life now and in the age to come.

title: Tree of Life
summary: In the opening pages of the Bible, God gives humanity a gift that they quickly forfeit: eternal life that comes by eating from the tree of life.

title: Blessing and Curse
summary: “Blessing” is a religious-sounding word that we use a lot. We say, “Bless you!” after a sneeze, or that we’re “so blessed” when life is good. But what does blessing mean in the Bible?

title: The Last Will Be First
summary: In the New Testament, Jesus is called the “firstborn,” a title of authority. While firstborns traditionally received inheritance and power in the ancient world, Jesus redefines this power.

title: The Test
summary: From the garden of Eden to the tempation of Jesus, the Bible shows a repeated theme of testing.

title: Water of Life
summary: In the beginning of the Bible, God transforms a desolate wilderness into a garden through a stream that waters the ground and brings life wherever it goes.

title: Sabbath
summary: The Bible opens with God creating an ordered world from chaos in six days before resting on the seventh day. This pattern of seven that ends with divine-human rest echoes throughout Scripture.

title: Generosity
summary: In the story of the Bible, God is depicted as a generous host who provides for the needs of his guests. However, humans live from a mindset of scarcity and hoard God’s many gifts.

title: Exile
summary: Exile is one of the core, yet often overlooked, themes underlying the entire biblical storyline. In this video, we'll see how Israel's exile to Babylon is a picture of all humanity's exile from Eden.

title: Temple
summary: The biblical authors describe Israel’s temple as the place where God’s space and human space overlap.

title: The Way of the Exile
summary: If followers of Jesus are to give their total allegiance to God’s Kingdom, how should they relate to the governments and power structures of their own day?

title: Justice
summary: Justice is a felt need in our world today and a controversial topic. But what is justice exactly, and who gets to define it?

title: Son of Man
summary: Why Jesus called himself the Son of Man.

title: Public Reading of Scripture
summary: Reading the Bible aloud with a group of people is an ancient practice. In fact, the origins of the Bible are rooted in public readings among members of the community.

title: Holy Spirit
summary: In this video, we explore the original meaning of the biblical concept of spirit (ruakh) and what it means that God’s Spirit is personally present in all of creation.

title: Image of God
summary: What does it mean for humans to be made in God’s image? In the opening pages of Genesis, we see God create humanity as his co-rulers of creation, but things quickly go wrong when humans rebel and forfeit their role.

title: Gospel of the Kingdom
summary: Gospel is a word that means “good news,” but it’s more than that. It’s a royal announcement, and its use in the New Testament points to the radical announcement of God’s Kingdom coming to Earth through Jesus.

title: The Law
summary: What is the importance of the ancient laws in the Hebrew Bible? Are they even relevant for Jesus followers? Explore how much the laws can teach us about God’s character and the significance of Jesus’ ministry on Earth.

title: Day of the Lord
summary: Does God still care about the destruction humans have caused in his good world? The story of the Bible shows us how God confronts human evil, as well as the deeper spiritual evil that is at work on Earth.

title: Sacrifice and Atonement
summary: God is on a mission to remove evil from his good world, along with all of its corrosive effects. However, he wants to do it in a way that doesn’t involve removing humans.

title: Holiness
summary: God’s holiness presents a paradox to human beings. God is the unique and set-apart Creator of all reality and the author of all goodness. However, that goodness can become dangerous to humans who are morally corrupt.

title: Covenants
summary: Despite human rebellion, God continues to make covenant promises to restore humanity to the role they were created for: to be partners with God in ruling creation.

title: The Messiah
summary: Explore the mysterious promise on page three of the Bible, that a promised deliverer would one day come to confront evil and rescue humanity.

title: Heaven & Earth
summary: What does the Bible really teach about Heaven, and what is Heaven’s relationship to Earth?

title: Exodus 34:6-7
summary: The list of God’s character traits found in Exodus 34:6-7 is the most repeated and re-quoted text in the Bible.

title: Khen / Grace
summary: Grace is a word we hear a lot in Christian circles, but the deeper meaning of this rich Hebrew word, especially how it relates to God's character, can get lost. In this video we look at what means for God to be gracious.

title: Khesed / Loyal Love
summary: The Hebrew word “khesed” is one of the most common descriptions of God in the Hebrew Bible, and it’s almost impossible to translate into any other language! This word combines the ideas of love, loyalty, and generosity.

title: Rakhamim / Compassion
summary: In the Bible, “compassion” is a deeply emotional word used to convey the strong bond between a parent and their child. It’s also the first word God uses to describe himself in Exodus 34:6-7.

title: ’Erek ’Appayim / Slow to Anger
summary: In Exodus 34, God describes himself as being "slow to anger," but what does this mean? The literal translation is a Hebrew idiom that has the potential to make this description even more confusing to modern readers.

title: Emet / Faithfulness
summary: The word emet is a common word used to describe God in the Bible.

title: Shema / Listen
summary: The Shema prayer sums up God’s greatest command, “Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one, and as for you, you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength.” Begin your study of this ancient…

title: Ahavah / Love
summary: Love can be a confusing word in the English language. It's used to refer to everything from your feelings to your mom to your feelings about pizza. But the biblical authors had more than one word for love.

title: YHWH / LORD
summary: YHWH, Adonai, LORD, Jehovah–God seems to have a lot of names. So what exactly are we supposed to call him?

title: Lev / Heart
summary: Different cultures have different conceptions of the human heart, what it is, and what it does.

title: Meod / Strength
summary: What does it mean to love God with all of your strength? In this final installment of our Shema series, we explore the Hebrew word me'od, which we translate as "strength" in the Shema.

title: Nephesh / Soul
summary: The English word “soul” usually refers to the non-material essence of a human that survives after death, but “nephesh” means something different.

title: Yakhal / Hope
summary: Biblical hope is not optimism. In fact, the most hopeful people in the Bible often had very few reasons to believe that things would get better for them any time soon.

title: Chara / Joy
summary: Explore the unique type of joy to which God’s people are called. It’s more than happy mood. It's a choice to trust that God will fulfill his promises, and it's a joy that is long-lasting and life-giving.

title: Shalom / Peace
summary: Peace is a very common word in English, and it means different things to different people.

title: Agape / Love
summary: The word “love” is one of the sloppiest words in our language, as it primarily refers to a feeling that happens to a person.

title: Khata / Sin
summary: The word sin is one of the most common bad words in the Bible, but what does it really mean? In this video, we’ll explore the concept of moral failure that underlies this important biblical word.

title: Pesha / Transgression
summary: Transgression is one of those bibilical words that seems clear until you have to explain it to somebody. In this video, we'll explore the fascinating and sophisticated meaning of this biblical bad word.

title: Avon / Iniquity
summary: Iniquity is a biblical word that very few people use anymore, and even fewer people know what it means!

title: Euangelion / Gospel
summary: Gospel is one of the most common words in a Christian’s vocabulary. But what does it mean in the original languages of the Bible?

title: What Is Passover?
summary: Watch a short video that explains the Hebrew meaning of the name for Passover and the story behind one of the Bible’s most important festivals.

title: Martus / Witness
summary: In the Bible, “witness” refers to both people and actions—those who see events and those who share what they’ve seen. Similar to today, this word is used in both legal settings and to describe an experience with God.

title: Nissah / Test
summary: The Hebrew word nissah, usually translated as “test,” describes an opportunity to have the truth about yourself revealed.

title: Kavod / Glory
summary: The Hebrew word glory ("kavod") describes a physical heaviness or social weightiness.

title: Mishkan / Dwelling Place
summary: Watch a short, animated video that explains the meaning of the Hebrew word for “dwelling” in key Bible verses.

title: Kopher / Ransom
summary: Watch a short, animated video that explains the meaning of the Hebrew word for "ransom" or "redemption payment" in the Bible.

title: Midbar / Wilderness
summary: The Hebrew word midbar describes a harsh wilderness that is resistant to life.

title: Ga’al / Redeem
summary: Watch a short, animated video that explains the meaning of the Hebrew word for "to redeem" in the Bible.

title: ’Avad / Serve, Work
summary: Watch a short, animated video that explains the meaning of the Hebrew word for “serve” or “worship” used in key Bible verses.

title: Zakar / Remember
summary: Watch a short, animated video that explains the meaning of the Hebrew word for “remember” used in key Bible verses.

title: ’Ot / Sign
summary: Watch a short, animated video that explains the meaning of the Hebrew word for “sign” used in key Bible verses.

title: Tse’aqah / Outcry
summary: Watch a short, animated video that explains the meaning of the Hebrew words for “outcry” used in key Bible verses.

title: Speck in the Eye

title: How does God respond to crooked human behavior?
summary: God responds to people and the twisted world we've created by making everything right.

title: The Hebrew word for iniquity describes distorted behavior and its crooked consequences.
summary: The word “iniquity” comes from the Hebrew word “avon,” which means bent or crooked. The Hebrew prophets use this image of crookedness as a powerful way of talking about people's behavior.

title: What happens when something that's supposed to be level or even gets bent out of shape?
summary: The word “iniquity” comes from the Hebrew word “avon,” which means bent or crooked. The Hebrew prophets use this image of crookedness as a powerful way of talking about people's behavior.

title: The Bible is one long story about a broken relationship
summary: Acts of pesha violate the universal trust that exists between all humans made in the image of God.

title: What Hebrew word describes the betrayal of a relationship?
summary: The Hebrew word "pesha" describes the betrayal of a relationship. Pesha is used repeatedly throughout the Bible as humans continually betray their covenant relationship with God and violate one another’s trust.

title: Here's the surprising twist in the Bible's story...
summary: Instead of letting humanity destroy itself, God took responsibility for our betrayal. By taking our pesha on himself, God opened up a new future and new way to be human.

title: What the Word Sin Actually Means
summary: In the Bible, the word “sin” means failing to fulfill a goal. But what's the goal? The goal is to love God and people by treating them with the honor they deserve.

title: Sin means redefining our bad decisions as good
summary: The word "sin" means missing the goal of loving God and people. Sin leads us to deceive ourselves. And in the Bible, when people are failing at loving God, they often think they are succeeding.

title: Failing to honor God is deeply connected to failing to honor people.
summary: The word "sin" means missing the goal of loving God and people. And a sin against people is a sin against God because failing to love a human made in God's image is a failure to love God.

title: How Does God "Remember"?
summary: We're told that God hears the cries of his people and remembers them. But God didn’t forget his people—because the Hebrew word for "remember" means more.

title: This Biblical Hebrew Word Means "Sign"
summary: The Hebrew word for "sign,  'ot (אֹת), points to a greater reality while containing a reality within itself. 🤔 In the Exodus story, both Moses' serpent-staff and the blood on the door during Passover act as signs.

title: In biblical Hebrew, hope is about waiting with expectation.
summary: The Hebrew word "qavah" comes from the word that means to pull a rope tight. When we qavah, we’re waiting with tense expectation.

title: The Hebrew word “he'imin” means to consider someone trustworthy or to trust.
summary: Abraham trusted God to fulfill his promises and open a way forward.

title: Ruakh = God's personal presence or Spirit
summary: Many Christian traditions celebrate the birth of the Church on Pentecost Sunday, when God's Spirit, or Ruakh, arrived with a rush of wind and "tongues" of fire.

title: Christ is a title, not a name.
summary: "Christ" means “anointed one.” And Christians are people marked by God's Spirit—anointed ones who follow the anointed one.

title: Compassion
summary: In Exodus 34:6, the first word used to describe God is compassionate. To be compassionate, it's not enough to see someone's pain. True compassion is seeing the suffering of others AND taking action to stop it.

title: What does joy look like in the Bible?
summary: In the story of the Bible, joy is an attitude God’s people adopt because of their hope in his promises—even though they face many challenging situations.

title: Why was Jesus’ birth announced as the arrival of peace?
summary: Jesus came to offer peace to others.

title: What does it mean to meditate on Scripture?
summary: In the Bible, meditating means slowly speaking or thinking about Scripture as a way to focus our attention until the words become part of us. Psalm 1 is a reflection on how what we meditate on shapes our path in life.

title: What does “holy” mean?
summary: In the Lord’s Prayer, Jesus asks for God’s name to be recognized as holy, meaning unique and honored.

title: Why does the Bible talk about Jesus as a temple?
summary: When the Bible talks about Jesus as a "dwelling place,” it is the same term used to refer to a tabernacle or temple. In Jesus, Heaven and Earth overlap just like in those sacred spaces.

title: What human power system does God consistently overturn in the Bible?
summary: In many cultures, inheritance and authority are passed down to the firstborn child.

title: Who does God regularly choose instead of the firstborn?
summary: In the story of the Bible, we consistently see God choosing the second-born or latecomer to receive his blessing.

title: What happens when humans join the rebellious creature in Genesis 3?
summary: The creature in Genesis 3 is in a state of rebellion against God. And when humans join with the creature, they are dragged back into disorder, chaos, and death.

title: Where does the rebellious creature in Genesis 3 go after the garden?
summary: The Bible offers subtle clues that this creature continues working behind the scenes to drag creation back into darkness and disorder.

title: What happens when humans choose to redefine good and evil by their own terms?
summary: The Bible tells the story of humans choosing to redefine good and evil by their own terms and act as if they are God. The result? Broken relationships and violence.

title: What is the Curse?
summary: When humans choose to seize God's blessing on their own, the curse enters the world. Watch "What is the Curse?"

title: What's the Difference Between the Two Trees in the Garden?
summary: Two trees represent the decision between trusting God's blessing or seizing abundance on our own. Watch now.

title: What Is the Bible's First Blessing?
summary: The story of the Bible opens with God creating a beautiful world and appointing humans to care for it. Watch "What Is the Bible's First Blessing?"

title: What Is God's blessing?
summary: When God blesses humans, he invites them to share his life-producing abilities and flourish. Watch "What Is God's Blessing?"

title: What does cosmology mean?
summary: Cosmology refers to the words or imagery used to describe the ordered world. When we read Genesis 1, we are introduced to the cosmology of the biblical authors.

title: Who were the Nephilim, and why didn't ancient readers find them strange?
summary: The ancient Israelites believed that their neighboring kingdoms were founded by giant warrior kings who were part-god and part-human.The Bible explains that the reason these kings spread violence is because they were captive to spiritual evil.

title: What does God tell Cain?
summary: Cain kills his brother out of jealousy, and then he builds the first city in the Bible to protect himself from increasing violence. God warns Cain that sin is a monster that wants to consume him, but he can rule it.

title: What makes the city different from the garden?
summary: In the Bible, the city’s purpose is self-preservation. It’s a place where peace is enforced by the threat of death. But the culture of the garden is peace through generosity.

title: What does God give Abraham and Sarah?
summary: Beginning with Abraham and Sarah, God plans to restore his blessing through one family. Watch now.

title: Hagar in the Wilderness
summary: Hagar’s story challenges Brittany on our Scholarship team to see how God helps people flourish even while spending a lifetime in the wilderness.

title: Where did the first anointing happen in the Bible?
summary: The practice of anointing with oil is an ancient ritual that marked people and places as bridges between Heaven and Earth.

title: The Blood of the Lamb
summary: The phrase “blood of the lamb” has an origin story. Do you know it?

title: Israel, Pharaoh, and Redemption
summary: God saving the ancient Israelites from Pharaoh’s oppression is an example of redemption.

title: Water of Life in the Wilderness
summary: Watch our Water of Life video to understand how God provides for his people in the wilderness—and then rescues them from it.

title: The Stinky Cheese on the Sinai Hamburger
summary: The middle section of the Sinai narrative contains the story's most disappointing moment—the people decide they don't want to go near God.

title: How Does God Respond to His People’s Fear of the Mountain?
Wisdom in the 1st Commandment
summary: When we give our allegiance to any power other than God, it can destroy us.

title: Wisdom in the 2nd Commandment: No Idols
summary: When we try to contain God or shape him into something familiar, we end up distorting the truth about God and ourselves.

title: Can sin be in God's presence?
summary: God designed the tabernacle to move toward sin in order to redeem it and invite people to enter his presence.

title: The ancient recipe for anointing oil does not include … pine sap.
summary: Tim and Jon discuss the ancient recipe for anointing oil which includes spices and myrrh, a substance extracted from the gum of trees.

title: Why objects were anointed in the Old Testament
summary: The practice of anointing with oil is an ancient ritual that marked people and places as bridges between Heaven and Earth.

title: The Year of Jubilee and Redemption
summary: What are two examples of redemption? A bad day that has turned good and the Year of Jubilee.

title: How do our choices shape us over time?
summary: Explore Psalm 1 in the Bible and reflect on three destructive ways of being human.

title: What are two ways of being human?
summary: Psalm 1 tells us that every human has a choice between two paths. One path leads to life, while the other path leads to ruin.

title: Who will rebuild creation?
summary: Isaiah 61 talks about a group of people who will rebuild creation and bring restoration—they’re called the anointed ones.

title: Who was Isaiah 61 written to encourage?
summary: Israel had been conquered and driven out of their land. And Isaiah’s words are meant to encourage the small group of Israelites who continue to trust in God's promises even as they mourn.

title: What does a restored world look like?
summary: In Isaiah 61, the prophet shares a vision of a restored world. The land is filled with abundance and ordered by right relationships.

title: Why Does Daniel Dream About Monsters?
summary: The four monstrous beasts in Daniel's dream represent four violent kingdoms. Daniel’s dream continues with the arrival of the Son of Man, who shows up to destroy the beasts.

title: What Do Dragons Represent in the Bible?
summary: Biblical authors used dragon imagery to represent chaos, darkness, and violent human rulers.

title: How Does Jesus Resist the Dragon?
summary: Jesus resists the dragon in a surprising way—he surrenders to it.

title: The Gospel of Matthew and the Exodus Way
summary: In Matthew’s gospel, Jesus walks the exodus way. His baptism marks the way out. His wilderness testing shows the way through. And finally, his transformative ministry of healing and teaching that reveals the way in.

title: Why was Jesus anointed with water instead of oil?
summary: Israel's priests and kings were anointed with oil to set them apart as leaders and God's representatives. But Jesus was anointed with water and Spirit because he is the ultimate Anointed One.

title: What was life like for the people listening to Jesus?
summary: Many of the people living in the hills of Galilee had lost their land to Rome. They were poor, powerless, and struggling to get by.

title: God's Kingdom begins here.
summary: Why does the Sermon on the Mount start the way it does? 🤔

title: Jesus wants the crowd listening to his sermon to know something important.
summary: Israel's prophets said that one day, God's heavenly Kingdom would break in, starting with a small group of Israelites. The people listening to Jesus' Sermon on the Mount are part of this legacy.

title: Jesus describes a new reality that sounds beyond us—but it is starting here and now.
summary: Jesus claims that Heaven is coming to Earth, starting with the crowd listening to him.

title: What Does Jesus Claim About God's Blessing?
summary: Jesus announces that God's blessing is arriving in a new way. Watch "What Does Jesus Claim About God's Blessing?"

title: Why did Jesus call his followers a "city on a hill"?
summary: Jerusalem was an image of God's garden city for a time. But when Jesus announces the arrival of God's Kingdom, he doesn't even go to Jerusalem.

title: Why Does Jesus Compare Name-Calling to Murder?
summary: Jesus is revealing the wisdom underneath the commands of the Torah. Anger, verbal abuse, and murder are all outward behaviors that reflect how much we value someone else’s existence.

title: What does avoiding oaths have to do with peacemaking?
summary: Jesus teaches that peacemaking begins with a radical commitment to honesty and integrity. He tells his followers to honor others by keeping their word.

title: How does Jesus unpack an ancient law of retaliation and take its wisdom to a new level?
summary: "An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth" is a famous line from ancient law, intended to protect people from disproportionate retaliation.

title: How can we make sure our generosity is done out of love?
summary: Jesus doesn’t describe one right way to give generously. Instead, he encourages his followers to cultivate a close relationship with God and do right for the right reasons.

title: Instead of Giving a Rule About Prayer, Jesus Offers This Wisdom
summary: Prayer is about spending time with God. And the Bible describes Jesus praying alone and with his followers. But Jesus instructs his followers to pray to God in secret if praying in front of others leads to hypocrisy.

title: Can We Enter God’s Kingdom Now?
summary: Jesus prays for the reunion of Heaven and Earth. But he also teaches his followers how to enter God’s Kingdom now through loving God and neighbor.

title: Why Does Jesus Pray About Bread?
summary: Jesus’ first audience was filled with people who often didn’t have enough to eat.

title: How is forgiveness like breathing?
summary: In his prayer, Jesus teaches his followers that in order to receive forgiveness, we must offer forgiveness. What goes in, must go out.

title: "If we don't forgive others, will God not forgive us?"
summary: We respond to this question and more in our fourth Question and Response episode in our Sermon on the Mount series. Tune in for some special bonus content from our listeners. (Hint: 🎵).

title: Why Say “Kingdom of the Skies” Instead of “Kingdom of Heaven?”
summary: Our BibleProject translation uses the phrase  “kingdom of the skies” instead of kingdom of heaven.” Discover why in our newest Q+R podcast episode.

title: Jesus Feeds People in the Wilderness
summary: Jesus surprises the crowd with an abundance of food in an unexpected place.

title: How does Jesus redefine power?
summary: Jesus claimed that God's power was arriving on Earth through him. But he redefined power as love and taught that if you want to be first, you need to become last.

title: How does Jesus define power?
summary: Jesus says that if you want to be first, you must be last. Real authority belongs to those who serve others.

title: "I was watching Satan fall from heaven like lightning."
summary: In Luke 10:17, Jesus describes how his followers can be victorious over spiritual rebels.

title: How Does God’s Spirit at Pentecost Offer Us Hope?
summary: The story of the Bible points to a new world filled with God's life-giving Spirit.

title: Fire + Wind = God’s Presence + Formation of a Temple
summary: Throughout the Hebrew Bible, fire and windstorms are connected to the arrival of God’s presence and the establishment of a new temple.

title: How Does Jesus' Death Reverse the Curse?
summary: Jesus dies under the curse but God reverses death by raising him back to life. Watch "How Does Jesus' Death Reverse the Curse?"

title: How did Jesus use his power?
summary: Jesus' earliest followers called him the firstborn of all creation–Jesus had enough power to bring the world into existence! But Jesus redefined how power could be used.

title: Generosity is central to the teachings of Jesus.
summary: BibleProject CEO Steve Atkinson encourages you to give generously to organizations that are making a difference so that you may "take hold of the life that is truly life."

title: Can We Be Royal Priests?
summary: Followers of Jesus embrace their calling as royal priests by sharing his love, serving those in need, and interceding in prayer.

title: Who Gets the Blessing in God's New World?
summary: The biblical story closes with all people sharing God's blessing and abundance. Watch now.

title: What is the focus of the Bible's story?
summary: The biblical story focuses on reuniting Heaven and Earth so that God's space and human space overlap again.

title: Do some Old Testament narratives make you uncomfortable?
summary: Biblical narratives have been misused to promote violent conquests throughout history. But when we read the Bible through the lens of Jesus' upside-down Kingdom, we discover a different story.

title: What does Jesus do with his authority?
summary: Jesus shares his authority and power with his followers so that they can form a new kind of family. Instead of being filled with feuds and rivalries, this family is ordered by Jesus' redefinition of power as love.

title: What caused Jesus to confront leaders?
summary: In the Bible, Jesus challenges Israel's leaders for abusing their power.

title: How does the Bible talk about demons?
summary: In the Bible demons are dark spiritual forces that can drag God's good creation into chaos and darkness.

title: Are you confused when you read the Old Testament?
summary: Dr. Tim Mackie explains a helpful step for understanding the Old Testament.

title: Biblical hope is based on a person.
summary: People express hope throughout the Bible, and most often what they hope for is God himself.

title: What does biblical hope look like?
What is biblical hope?
summary: Christian hope is a choice to wait for God to bring about the future he has promised.

title: What is the Day of the Lord?
summary: The Day of the Lord is the future and final day when God will overcome evil and make everything new.

title: Is There a Right Way To Read the Bible?
summary: The Bible isn't a rule book. It tells the story of God making humans his partners, humans ruining it, and God restoring the world through Jesus. #shorts #BibleProject #biblevideo #bible

title: Where Are We on the Exodus Way?
summary: Today, we’re walking through the wilderness, where we learn to trust God and his promise to make everything new.

title: How do God's space and human space overlap?
summary: In the Bible, Heaven and Earth describe God's space and human space. In the story of the Bible, these two spaces have been torn apart—but Jesus has the power to reunite them.

title: How can we experience moments when Heaven and Earth overlap?
summary: Jesus teaches that we can experience God's heavenly Kingdom now when we love God and love our neighbor.

title: Can Heaven Happen Here?
summary: The union of Heaven and Earth is at the center of the biblical story. They have been separated, but God is bringing them together.

title: Is God's garden city realistic?
summary: Jerusalem is the image of God's heavenly city for a time. This garden city represents God's plan for his people to live in peace through generosity, but the city is eventually conquered by Babylon.

title: How do we transform the mindset of Cain's city?
summary: The mindset of Cain's city is self-preservation and peace enforced by the threat of death. And the only way we overcome the fear of death is by trusting in the one who is stronger than death.

title: What did the biblical prophets write about?
summary: The prophets showed how Israel failed to live by God’s wisdom and follow his laws.

title: Jesus’ compassion moves him to enter into death itself to rescue us and bring us near to God.
summary: Human suffering deeply moves Jesus. So much so that he gave his life to rescue us all. See the full video and more related resources here:

title: Generosity
summary: God’s generous love turns death into life and scarcity into abundance.

title: God Is a Generous Host
summary: Even with all the gifts we've been given, there are times when we feel they aren't enough. Just like the Israelites, we can forget the Promised Land God has gifted us and begin to live in fear.

title: How Does Jesus Show Us How to Love?
Genesis and the Exodus Way
summary: Follow the exodus way design pattern in the book of Genesis: the way out of slavery, the way through the wilderness, and the way into a new land.

title: Isaiah and the Exodus Way
summary: Follow the exodus way design pattern in the book of Isaiah: the way out of slavery, the way through the wilderness, and the way into the promised land.

title: Redemption and Economic Words
summary: Why is the language of debt, purchasing, and redeeming part of how Christians talk about Jesus?

title: Biblical Settings and the Wilderness
summary: Biblical authors use settings to draw out emotions and build expectations. When we read a story, we naturally connect each scene to similar stories we’ve encountered before.

title: What If There's No List to Follow?
summary: Meditating on the Bible as wisdom literature shapes our decision-making—especially when there’s no list of instructions or rules for a particular situation.

title: Why Rules Aren't Enough
summary: The Bible is wisdom literature, and understanding it as a rulebook limits how it can shape our lives.
